testSuites.details: 911 tests completed, 1 failed, 2 skipped. The single failure is com.botfunnel.webhook.TelegramWebhookP99IT#p99Latency_under100msAt100ParallelRequests — a hard-coded P99 < 100ms latency assertion over 100 parallel HTTP requests against a real Spring Boot + Testcontainers Mongo stack. Created in the webhook-ingestion epic (commit f2664d5), NOT modified by the funnels feature (verified: be0282f..HEAD shows no change to this file). Every funnel-scoped backend test is green.

testSuites.name: Frontend unit (Vitest)
testSuites.details: 47 files, 368 tests passed. Includes funnel-scoped specs: tests/components/FunnelStepsList.spec.ts (3), tests/stores/funnels.spec.ts (10), plus i18n required-keys parity.

testSuites.name: Frontend E2E (Playwright)
testSuites.details: Initial run (backend NOT running): 2 failed (i18n, projects), 3 skipped. Root cause of the mass failure diagnosed and confirmed: the Nuxt dev server proxies /api -> localhost:8080 and the client-side auth.global middleware awaits fetchUser() during hydration; with the backend down that proxied call blocks Vue suspense indefinitely, so hydration never completes (probe: __vue_app__ never set after 60s, app non-interactive, ZERO JS errors). With the backend started, hydration completes in 0.6s and the app is fully interactive. funnels.spec.ts health-probes the backend and skips gracefully (Task 11 AC); i18n/projects specs lack that guard and hang instead. After bringing the backend up: i18n.spec.ts PASSES; projects.spec.ts still fails at a later step (see finding F2); funnels.spec.ts (2) and subscribers.spec.ts (1) skip for lack of live seed bootstrap.

findings.title: Backend perf test TelegramWebhookP99IT is flaky / environment-sensitive (non-funnel)
findings.expected: P99 latency < 100ms over 100 parallel webhook POSTs
findings.actual: 103ms under full-suite load; 559ms cold/isolated. Fails the suite (exit 1).
findings.scope: Out of funnel feature scope — created in the webhook-ingestion epic (commit f2664d5), untouched by 10-funnels.
findings.reproduction: cd backend && ./gradlew test -PrunSlow=true (or --tests 'com.botfunnel.webhook.TelegramWebhookP99IT'). Latency varies wildly with machine load and JVM warmup.
findings.recommendation: Owned by the webhook epic, not this feature. Make the threshold environment-aware (warmup iterations, percentile over more samples, or tag as a perf test excluded from the standard gate). Not a funnel blocker.

findings.title: projects.spec.ts golden path fails on email-verification gating (non-funnel, epic 05)
findings.expected: Freshly-registered user lands on /dashboard and sees the empty-state CTA (data-test=dashboard-empty-state-cta)
findings.actual: Dashboard shows only the 'Verify your email for full access' pending banner; showEmpty is false for a pending (unverified) user, so the empty-state CTA never renders -> 5s timeout.
findings.scope: Out of funnel feature scope — funnels did not touch dashboard.vue, the projects store, auth, or email verification (verified: be0282f..HEAD empty for those files). Task 15's only edit to this spec was an appended sidebar-link sanity assertion at step 10, unrelated to the failing line 61.
findings.reproduction: Backend up; cd frontend && pnpm test:e2e e2e/projects.spec.ts. Fresh register -> /en/dashboard shows pending banner, no empty-state CTA.
findings.recommendation: Owned by the projects/auth epics. Update the golden-path test to verify the email (or seed a verified user) before asserting the project empty-state, matching current auth gating. Not a funnel blocker.

findings.title: i18n.spec.ts uses waitForLoadState('networkidle'), which hangs in dev mode
findings.actual: networkidle never settles under Nuxt HMR WebSocket; the test only passes incidentally. projects.spec.ts already abandoned networkidle for the __vue_app__ hydration probe for exactly this reason (its own comment, commit e10067d).
findings.reproduction: Observed: i18n.spec timed out at waitForLoadState('networkidle') even though the page was fully rendered and interactive.
findings.recommendation: Replace networkidle with the same __vue_app__ hydration-gate probe used by projects.spec.ts. Passed once the backend was up in this run, but the wait is fragile.
